summary: Cross-language orchestration: partial tool execution observed after streaming client retry (TS client -> Python webhook)
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when using the TypeScript streaming SDK with multiplexed user sessions to drive a Python webhook-based tool, some tool invocations complete only partially (side-effect applied once) when the client reconnects and retries the streaming request. Impact: Duplicate or partial side-effects observed in downstream systems (orders partially created, one of two downstream webhooks fired). Customer is on a dedicated deployment in us-east and has pinned model redwood/gpt-compat-8k. Environment: prod (dedicated), SDK versions: sdk-js@2.8.1 (streaming + multiplex), sdk-py@1.4.0 (webhook handler), ingress via api-gateway v1.3.2. Steps to reproduce (customer-provided): 1) Open a multiplexed streaming connection from the TS client and start two concurrent sessions on the same connection. 2) For session A, trigger a function call that posts to the customer's Python webhook (POST /tools/charge) with an idempotency header X-Redwood-Idempotency: <session-level-id>. 3) Mid-stream, simulate transient network loss (client reconnect/backoff) while the server has already accepted and forwarded the first tool call. 4) Client reconnects and resends the in-flight messages without attaching per-action idempotency metadata (only session-level id attached). 5) The Python handler performs a partial side-effect (writes to cache and schedules a downstream job) before the request fails; on the retried call the webhook sees the session id and treats it as the same logical session but is unable to detect per-action duplicates, leading to partial re-execution or missing compensations. Expected behavior: When the streaming client retries, downstream tool webhooks should either receive a stable per-action idempotency key so the webhook can deduplicate at action granularity, or the Redwood runtime should guarantee at-most-once forwarding semantics for accepted tool invocations. Actual behavior: Partial duplicate side-effects and orphaned downstream jobs for a subset (~3/50) of retried tool calls under customer load. Customer included request/response traces and webhook logs showing different request IDs but identical session id header. Logs/Trace snippets: - TS client reconnect log: "stream: reconnect attempt=1 inflight=2 session_id=usr-92ab" - Gateway forwarded request id: gw-20260310-8471 for first attempt, gw-20260310-8472 for retry - Webhook handler log: "received charge call action_id=None session_id=usr-92ab; started processing; wrote cache key order-123.tmp; error: upstream job enqueue timeout" - Later: "retry received action_id=None session_id=usr-92ab; enqueue succeeded; downstream job duplicate with partial state" Additional notes: Customer's Python handler relies on action-level idempotency token (X-Action-Id) but the TS client only attached session-level id for multiplexing optimization. The customer asks whether this is expected SDK behavior and how best to avoid partial side-effects.

investigation_notes: Checked gateway logs for gw-20260310-8471 / gw-20260310-8472; both forwarded to different runtime worker ids. No immediate evidence of duplicate forwarding suppression at runtime for session-only idempotency headers.

Observed Dedicated autoscaler activity and worker recycle that correlated with reconnect window. Worker A forwarded initial tool call to webhook; Worker B forwarded retry attempt after reconnect. Runtime does not currently synthesize per-action tokens when the client omits them.

Reproduced locally with sdk-js@2.8.1 multiplex example: when attaching only X-Session-Id, reconnect+resend results in two separate gw request ids and webhook sees two distinct attempts with same session id but no per-action id.

Reviewed Python webhook handler: it attempted to be idempotent using a composite key session_id + (action payload hash) but the payload hash differed because partial writes changed state between attempts leading to mismatched dedupe keys. This made dedupe fragile.

Hypothesis: The root cause is a combination of multiplexing optimization (clients omitting per-action ids), midstream worker handoff (due to autoscale/drain), and webhook dedupe strategy relying on mutable payloads rather than stable client-supplied action ids.
Severity assessment: P1 due to monetary side-effects but low frequency; recommend short-term mitigations and medium-term runtime/client improvements.
Correlated linked tickets for similar symptoms: SUP-29871 (stream replay duplicates), SUP-41209 (confirmation-token patterns).
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation provided to customer (03/12): 1) Update TS client to attach X-Action-Id per tool invocation (UUID v4) even when using multiplexed streams; 2) Webhook handler to persist seen X-Action-Id in a small atomic DB row before any mutable downstream changes; on duplicate attempts, return success without re-executing side-effects. Implementation guidance and example code snippet provided in reply.
Customer validated canary with 5000 requests and observed zero partial duplicates after adding per-action idempotency tokens. They will roll this change to production this week.

Medium-term product follow-ups opened: - Add runtime warning/logging when session-level-only idempotency header is detected on a streaming connection; - Docs update explaining per-action idempotency is required when using multiplexed streams that may reconnect; - Investigate runtime-level per-action id synthesis when client includes deterministic sequencing metadata (RFC/PR created).

Related PRs and docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/2410 (example to attach X-Action-Id in multiplex client), https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Idempotency+and+Retries+Runbook (updated section draft).

Follow-ups: Product to triage feature request in next planning cycle; Engineering to evaluate runtime guard complexity and false positives. Support to close ticket when customer confirms prod roll-out and no regressions after 72h.
Status: Waiting on customer rollout verification (target close if green by 2026-03-15).
